newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel reopens part of Hebron produce market.
newsitem.headline: Israel reopens part of Hebron produce market.

text.p: Israel, implementing another part of a peace deal with the PLO, on Wednesday reopened part of the produce market in the West Bank town of Hebron that had been closed since a Jewish settler massacred 29 Moslems three years ago, witnesses said.
They said senior Israeli officers looked on as municipal workers and owners reopened the stores and began cleaning them up.
"This is another stage of implementing the agreement with the Israeli side," said Tawfiq Arafeh, a Hebron municipality engineer who will supervise renovations of the market.
"This will make people feel that the agreements are being implemented and that life is gradually returning to normalcy," he said.
Israel handed over 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule. Some 400 Jewish settlers live or study amidst some 20,000 Palestinians in the rest of the town still controlled by Israel.

Israel also agreed to gradually reopen a main street linking both sides of town and the produce market which is located near a Jewish enclave in the Israeli-held part. Shuhada street was reopened to public transportation earlier this month.

Arafeh said only nine of the 17 shops in the market were being reopened in the first stage and they would only be used for retail trade. He said the shops would be handed over to owners after necessary renovations.
Israel closed the market after Jewish settler Baruch Goldstein massacred 29 Moslems kneeling in prayer at Hebron's al-Ibrahimi mosque in February 1994. He was beaten to death by the survivors.
